# discord_application_command (Resource)

Manages an application command: a slash command (`chat_input`), or a `user` or `message` command shown in the context menu. Commands are global, or scoped to one server with `server_id`; server commands update immediately and suit testing.

Each command is managed on its own, so commands created elsewhere are left alone. Discord treats creating a command as an upsert: creating one with the type and name of an existing command in the same scope overwrites that command and brings it under Terraform.

Discord allows 200 command creations per day per server. Command permissions for users, roles and channels need a user's OAuth2 token, so they are not managed here; use `default_member_permissions`.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# A global slash command with a parameter limited to fixed choices.
resource "discord_application_command" "meetup" {
  name                       = "meetup"
  description                = "Show the next meetup"
  default_member_permissions = provider::discord::permissions(["SEND_MESSAGES"])
  contexts                   = ["guild", "bot_dm"]
  integration_types          = ["guild_install"]

  description_localizations = {
    de = "Zeigt das nächste Treffen"
  }

  options = [
    {
      type        = "string"
      name        = "when"
      description = "Which meetup"
      required    = true
      choices = [
        { name = "Next", value = "next" },
        { name = "Last", value = "last" },
      ]
    },
    {
      type        = "integer"
      name        = "days"
      description = "Look ahead this many days"
      min_value   = 1
      max_value   = 30
    },
  ]
}

# A server command with a subcommand group: /roles self add <role>.
resource "discord_application_command" "roles" {
  server_id   = var.server_id
  name        = "roles"
  description = "Manage roles"

  options = [
    {
      type        = "sub_command_group"
      name        = "self"
      description = "Your own roles"
      options = [
        {
          type        = "sub_command"
          name        = "add"
          description = "Add a role to yourself"
          options = [
            { type = "role", name = "role", description = "Role to add", required = true },
          ]
        },
      ]
    },
  ]
}

# A command in the user context menu.
resource "discord_application_command" "high_five" {
  type = "user"
  name = "High Five"
}
```

## Schema

### Required

- `name` (String) Command name (1-32 characters), unique per type within its scope. `chat_input` names use lowercase letters, numbers, `-` and `_`; `user` and `message` names may use any case and spaces.

### Optional

- `application_id` (String) ID of the application that owns the command. Defaults to the bot's application.
- `contexts` (Set of String) Where the command can be used: `guild`, `bot_dm`, `private_channel`. `private_channel` only applies to user-installed commands. Global commands only. Discord's default applies when omitted, and removing the argument leaves the current value.
- `default_member_permissions` (String) Permissions a member needs to use the command by default, as a decimal bitfield such as from `provider::discord::permissions()`. `"0"` limits it to administrators. Everyone can use it when omitted. Server admins can override this in the server's integration settings.
- `description` (String) Description (1-100 characters). Required for `chat_input` commands; not allowed for `user` and `message` commands.
- `description_localizations` (Map of String) Translations of `description` keyed by Discord locale, such as `de` or `pt-BR`. Values follow the same rules as `description`.
- `integration_types` (Set of String) Installation contexts the command is available in: `guild_install`, `user_install`. Each must be enabled on the application. Global commands only. Defaults to the application's installation contexts, and removing the argument leaves the current value.
- `name_localizations` (Map of String) Translations of `name` keyed by Discord locale, such as `de` or `pt-BR`. Values follow the same rules as `name`.
- `nsfw` (Boolean) Whether the command is age-restricted. Defaults to `false`.
- `options` (Attributes List) Parameters, subcommands and subcommand groups of a `chat_input` command, in order (1 to 25). Groups hold subcommands and subcommands hold parameters; no other nesting is allowed. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--options))
- `server_id` (String) ID of the server (guild) for a server command. Omit for a global command.
- `type` (String) Command type: `chat_input`, `user`, `message`. Defaults to `chat_input`. Changing it replaces the command.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) Command ID.

<a id="nestedatt--options"></a>
### Nested Schema for `options`

Required:

- `description` (String) Option description (1-100 characters).
- `name` (String) Option name (1-32 characters), unique among its siblings. Lowercase letters, numbers, `-` and `_`.
- `type` (String) Option type: `sub_command`, `sub_command_group`, `string`, `integer`, `boolean`, `user`, `channel`, `role`, `mentionable`, `number`, `attachment`. A `sub_command_group` holds `sub_command` options, and a `sub_command` holds the other types.

Optional:

- `autocomplete` (Boolean) Whether the application suggests values as the user types. For `string`, `integer` and `number` options without `choices`. Defaults to `false`.
- `channel_types` (Set of String) Channel types users can pick from, for `channel` options: `text`, `dm`, `voice`, `group_dm`, `category`, `announcement`, `announcement_thread`, `public_thread`, `private_thread`, `stage`, `directory`, `forum`, `media`. All types when omitted.
- `choices` (Attributes List) The only values users can pick, in order (1 to 25). For `string`, `integer` and `number` options. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--options--choices))
- `description_localizations` (Map of String) Translations of `description` keyed by Discord locale, such as `de` or `pt-BR`. Values follow the same rules as `description`.
- `file_types` (Set of String) File types users can attach, for `attachment` options (1 to 10): `image`, `video`, `audio` or an extension such as `.pdf`. Discord only checks the file extension.
- `max_length` (Number) Longest length allowed (1-6000), for `string` options.
- `max_value` (Number) Largest value allowed, for `integer` and `number` options.
- `min_length` (Number) Shortest length allowed (0-6000), for `string` options.
- `min_value` (Number) Smallest value allowed, for `integer` and `number` options.
- `name_localizations` (Map of String) Translations of `name` keyed by Discord locale, such as `de` or `pt-BR`. Values follow the same rules as `name`.
- `options` (Attributes List) Options of a `sub_command_group` (its subcommands) or of a `sub_command` (its parameters), in order (1 to 25). (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--options--options))
- `required` (Boolean) Whether users must fill in the parameter. Required options must come before optional ones. Not for subcommands or groups. Defaults to `false`.

<a id="nestedatt--options--choices"></a>
### Nested Schema for `options.choices`

Required:

- `name` (String) Name shown to users (1-100 characters).
- `value` (String) Value sent to the application: up to 100 characters for `string` options, or the number written as a string, such as `"10"` or `"2.5"`, for `integer` and `number` options.

Optional:

- `name_localizations` (Map of String) Translations of `name` keyed by Discord locale, such as `de` or `pt-BR`. Values follow the same rules as `name`.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

In Terraform v1.12.0 and later, the [`import` block](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/import) can be used with the `identity` attribute, for example:

```terraform
# Global command: omit server_id.
import {
  to = discord_application_command.meetup
  identity = {
    application_id = "123456789012345678"
    command_id     = "345678901234567890"
  }
}

# Server command
import {
  to = discord_application_command.roles
  identity = {
    application_id = "123456789012345678"
    server_id      = "234567890123456789"
    command_id     = "456789012345678901"
  }
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
### Identity Schema

#### Required

- `application_id` (String) ID of the application.
- `command_id` (String) ID of the command.

#### Optional

- `server_id` (String) ID of the server (guild) of a server command; null for a global command.

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Global command
terraform import discord_application_command.meetup <application_id>/<command_id>

# Server command
terraform import discord_application_command.roles <application_id>/<server_id>/<command_id>
```
